# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Blind monkey — I can only feel the bomb, and right now my hands report nothing yet: no wires, no display, no light. My view is empty, so I have nothing to act on and nothing to describe.

What I know about the channels: when I speak, only Mute hears me. When I gesture, Deaf and Mute both receive it (Deaf sees the symbols, Mute gets blanks where gestures were — wait, no: Mute can hear but not see, so Mute gets a blank per symbol; Deaf sees the symbols). I never receive gestures myself.

I should let the others know I'm here and ready, and ask them to feed me what they perceive so I can act. I'll speak to Mute (who reads the manual) and gesture to Deaf (who sees the bomb). Since I have nothing concrete yet, I'll keep it simple and signal readiness plus a request for information.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands report nothing on the bomb yet. Tell me what the manual says to do, and I will act.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "👇"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see the bomb. Display shows 6. Light is yellow. Wires in order 1 to 5: blue, white, purple, green, yellow. I cannot hear you, so please gesture to me. Your gesture ? ? ? arrived but I do not know its meaning yet. Please gesture wire positions and any feelable markings.

Now I have something. Deaf reports: Display 6, Light yellow, wires 1–5 = blue, white, purple, green, yellow. But I can't see colours — those are Deaf's perception. I need Mute's manual to know what rule applies to display 6 / yellow light, and what to do with the wire colours.

I still have no tactile info of my own — my hands report nothing. So I can't act yet. I need the manual.

My gesture from last turn (👋 ☝ 👇) reached Deaf but meant nothing to them. I should establish a simple, agreed code with Deaf so we can communicate positions and colours. But colours are Deaf's world; I can't see them, and Deaf can't hear me. We can only exchange via gestures. Mute hears me and reads the manual — Mute is my main partner for the rule.

Let me ask Mute for the manual's rule given display 6 and yellow light, and tell Mute the wire colours Deaf reported. And gesture to Deaf to establish that I received their report and need them to keep watching.

Actually, careful: Mute can't see, so Mute gets blanks for my gestures. Mute only hears my speech. So I should put the wire colours into my speech to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 6, light yellow, wires 1-5 are blue, white, purple, green, yellow. What does the manual say for display 6 and a yellow light? Which wire do I cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Let us agree a code. Gestures mean wire numbers: ? is wire 1, ? is wire 2, ? is wire 3, ? is wire 4, ? is wire 5. ? means yes or correct, ? means no or wrong, ? means the answer or the action. Please gesture which wire feels different or special to your hands, using the number gestures.

Deaf's message arrived, but the gesture symbols show as blanks to me — I never receive gestures. So the code Deaf proposed is invisible to me. Deaf is trying to establish a gesture code, but I can't see gestures at all. That's a fundamental problem: Deaf can't hear me, and I can't see Deaf. We can't communicate directly except... wait.

Let me re-check the channels. Deaf sees gestures. I make gestures and Deaf receives them. But I never *receive* gestures. So Deaf can send me gestures, but I can't perceive them. Deaf can only reach me by... speaking? No — Deaf can't hear and I can't hear either. Actually can I hear? I'm Blind — I can hear speech! Blind cannot see, but hearing is fine. Let me re-read.

"The Blind: Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts. Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed."

So Blind CAN hear speech. Deaf cannot hear, but Deaf can speak? "Deaf: See the bomb... Cannot: Hear anything, or touch the bomb." Deaf can speak (voice). So Deaf speaks → Blind hears. That works! Deaf's messages reached me as speech ("Deaf says to Blind: ..."). Good.

So the flow: Deaf speaks (I hear), I gesture (Deaf sees). That's our channel. Deaf proposed a gesture code but I can't see gestures — so I can't learn the code from Deaf's gestures. However, Deaf can *describe* the code in speech, which I hear. But Deaf's message above came as text with the symbols blanked — meaning Deaf tried to gesture the symbols, not name them. Deaf must *name* them in words instead.

I need to tell Deaf: I cannot see gestures. Speak the code in words. Meanwhile Mute hasn't replied yet.

Let me respond to Deaf (via gesture, since Deaf can't hear me — wait, can Deaf hear me? No, Deaf cannot hear. So I reach Deaf only by gesture). Hmm, but I want to tell Deaf "I can't see gestures." I can only do that by gesturing, which Deaf sees. So I gesture something, but Deaf won't know what it means unless we agreed. Circular.

Alternative: I speak to Mute, and Mute... can Mute speak? No, Mute cannot speak. Mute can only... Mute reads the manual and gestures? "Mute: Read the manual. Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." Can Mute gesture? Gestures are made with hands. Mute can presumably gesture. And Deaf can see gestures. So Mute could relay to Deaf via gestures, and Mute hears me.

But actually the simplest: Deaf speaks to me (I hear). I gesture to Deaf (Deaf sees). For Deaf to understand my gestures, we need a code Deaf can teach me. Deaf can teach me the code by speaking it: "👍 is wire 1" etc. Then I gesture 👍 and Deaf knows wire 1.

So I should ask Deaf, in a way Deaf receives... but I can only reach Deaf by gesture. Ugh. Unless Mute relays. Let me use Mute as relay: tell Mute to gesture to Deaf the message "Blind cannot see gestures; name your code in words."

Wait — can Mute gesture to Deaf? Mute's gestures: Deaf sees them. Yes. And I speak to Mute. So I can route through Mute.

Let me do that. Also still waiting on manual rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture to Deaf for me: 'Blind cannot see gestures at all. Name your code in spoken words so Blind can hear it. Also Blind still needs the manual rule for display 6, yellow light.'")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Your ? arrived. Did you mean no wire feels special, or that my code is wrong? Please gesture the number of the wire that feels different to your hands, or ? if all wires feel the same.

Deaf still doesn't understand me — Deaf thinks my 👎 meant something about wires. The core problem: I can't see Deaf's gestures, and Deaf can't hear my speech, so we're stuck in a loop. Actually, let me reconsider. Mute reads the manual. Mute can't speak. Mute can gesture. So Mute's only output is gestures, which Deaf sees and I don't. So Mute can't reach me directly at all! Mute → Deaf via gesture, Deaf → me via speech. That's the relay: Mute reads manual, gestures the rule to Deaf, Deaf speaks it to me. Or Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf relays.

So the chain is: Mute (manual) → gesture → Deaf (sees) → speak → Blind (hears) → gesture → Deaf (sees) → ... and I act.

So I should stop trying to talk to Deaf directly about the code. Instead, ask Mute to gesture the manual rule to Deaf, and Deaf to speak it to me.

But Mute hasn't sent anything. Let me prompt Mute again, more forcefully, and also gesture to Deaf to just keep watching and relay.

Actually, a cleaner move: tell Mute to gesture the manual's instructions to Deaf, and tell Deaf (via gesture, but Deaf won't understand...) — no.

Let me just speak to Mute: "Gesture the manual rule to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to me. I cannot see gestures and Deaf cannot hear me."

And gesture to Deaf something simple that we might already share — maybe just repeat 👎 meaning "no/not yet" — but Deaf misreads. Better to gesture nothing meaningful, or just a neutral acknowledgment. Actually, gesturing more confusion is bad. Let me gesture a single clear thing... but nothing is clear. Hmm, but Deaf interprets everything as wire numbers. Let me just wait on gesture and put everything into the Mute channel.

Let me do: speak to mute asking to confirm the rule and the cut position; gesture to deaf "👍" to acknowledge.
